dva-ini-026.text: An application allows users to upload photos directly to a pocket S3 private, without the files passing through the application server. How the backend can authorize each upload securely and temporarily?

Asking users to send photos by email to support
Distributing account access keys in the application code
Generating a presigned URL uploading (PUT) with the SDK and delivering it to the customer for direct delivery to S3
dva-ini-026.explanation: Insignificant URL embeds a temporary authorization signed by the backend credentials: the client sends the file directly to S3 within the deadline, without exposing the pocket or overloading the server.

optionRationales: Insignificant URL embeds a temporary authorization signed by the backend credentials: the client sends the file directly to S3 within the deadline, without exposing the pocket or overloading the server.
Encapsulated credentials in the client app leak easily — severe security failure.
Public writing Bucket becomes the target of abuse and malicious storage — never the solution.
Manual process without scale or integration — not an engineering solution.

dva-ini-027.text: A developer needs to send to S3 video files from several gigabytes from the application, with parallelism and recovery of parts that fail. API of the S3 (automated by SDKs) is recommended for these uploads?
options: Single upload with larger timeout
Send via e-mail to support the AWS import
Multipart upload, dividing the file into parts sent in parallel
Split video into several small objects manually
dva-ini-027.explanation: Multipart upload is the mechanism of S3 for large objects: independent parts sent in parallel, isolated retransmission of failures and better throughput — SDKs automatically use it above certain sizes.
dva-ini-027.hint: Break in 'multiple parts', go up in parallel, S3 mounts the puzzle at the end.
optionRationales: Multipart upload is the mechanism of S3 for large objects: independent parts sent in parallel, isolated retransmission of failures and better throughput — SDKs automatically use it above certain sizes.
A single monolithic flow starts from scratch to every failure and does not take advantage of parallelism — fragile for gigabytes.
Fragmentation of the final object complicates consumption — the multipart joins parts into an object automatically at completion.
There is no e-mail import — the way is API of the S3.

dva-ini-033.text: What is the fundamental difference between the Query and Scan operations of DynamoDB, and why documentation recommends prefer Query whenever possible?
options: Query searches for items by partition key (reading only the target partition); Scan reads the entire table by filtering later — so Query is much more efficient and cheap
Scan is faster because it reads parallel by default
They're identical, changing only the name in SDK
Query only works on tables with less than 1 GB
dva-ini-033.explanation: Query navigates directly to the partition of the informed key; the Scan runs through all the items in the table consuming capacity proportional to the total read — in large tables, the difference in cost and latency is enormous.
dva-ini-033.hint: One goes straight to the right drawer through the key; the other opens all drawers and filters at the end.
optionRationales: Query navigates directly to the partition of the informed key; the Scan runs through all the items in the table consuming capacity proportional to the total read — in large tables, the difference in cost and latency is enormous.
Even with parallel scan, the operation continues to read the entire table — structural efficiency lower than targeted search.
There is no size limit for Query — it scales just by reading only the relevant partition.
They are operations with semantics and completely different costs.

dva-ini-034.text: A payment endpoint can receive the same request twice (e.g. client twice clicking or automatic retry of the SDK). Idempotence: the repeated operation produces the same result — implemented, for example, with a unique requisition identifier verified before performing the effects
Pagination: process requests in pages
Atomicity: divide the collection into two halves
dva-ini-034.explanation: Idempotent operations can be safely repeated; register an idempotency key (e.g. conditionally in the DynamoDB) and ignoring duplicates is the standard for integrations with recesses.
dva-ini-034.hint: Press the elevator button ten times does not call it ten times — what is the name of this property?
optionRationales: Idempotent operations can be safely repeated; register an idempotency key (e.g. conditionally in the DynamoDB) and ignoring duplicates is the standard for integrations with recesses.
Elasticity deals with capacity — does not prevent duplicate effects of repeated requests.
Atomicity guarantees 'everything or nothing' in a transaction — does not deal with the repetition of the whole operation.
Split Pagination RESULTADOS large blocks — irrelevant for duplication of execution.
